items.title: 54271_Charlie Holmes oral history interview
items.q: The person to judge is 'Harlem', which is a place, not a person. The interviewee discusses working for Vernon Andrade in Harlem, but does not describe a personal relationship with 'Harlem' as an individual.

ctx.x: Andrade. Vernon Andrade. He was the leader of the band. He stayed there for years. Yeah, Vernon Andrade, that's right.
It seems like if you hung around Harlem long enough, you'd eventually work for him.

Yeah, eventually you'd wind up working for him. That's right. Because I mean, they were coming and going in his band all the time. I mean, his band, he had no aspirations for going any place or doing anything. But he had a job. And that was the name of the game in them days -- a job. So different fellows, they'd be working or rehearsing in the big-time bands. Like Chick Webb's band, you'd be rehearsing with Chick Webb, but Chick wasn't doing anything, so they'd go to work with Vernon Andrade until the other band…
